title: Per-budget advice subtracts the whole organization's forecast from a single budget's remaining amount
impact: Example: the organization forecast is income PHP 20,000 and expense PHP 40,000, and the untouched 'Sportsfest' budget has PHP 10,000 left. The calculation is available = 10,000 + 20,000 - 40,000 = -10,000, so the result is 'deficit', high risk, no_funds and a safe limit of 0 for a healthy budget. In the opposite case a budget about to overrun is marked stable because org income lifts it. The result is written to budgets.overspending_risk, recommended_allocation and safe_spending_limit, and shown on the Finance page, the dashboard insight and in financial reports.
suggested_fix: Build the per-budget payload from that budget alone: current = recomputedRemaining(), predicted expense = the budget's own expense run rate or remaining planned spend (or 0), predicted income = income posted against that budget. Alternatively scale the org forecast by the budget's share of approved allocations. Put the forecast period and the inputs actually used in the response, and show them in the 'How this was calculated' disclosure.
verifier_notes: BudgetController::advice (line 225-233) builds the payload from the org-wide FinancialForecast::latestFor plus this single budget remaining_amount; advise_budget/localBudgetAdvice compute available = current + income - expense, so the scope mismatch is exactly as described, and the result is written to the budget row.

title: Forecast series stops at the last month with transactions, so trailing zero months are dropped and old history is extrapolated
impact: If an organization recorded income in Jan-Mar 2026 and nothing from April to October, the November generate fits a line through three points and projects it nine months ahead to December. The seven real zero months are missing from the series, so income can be inflated or swing far outside the data. sample_months reads 3, so the warning blames a short history rather than inactivity. The available funds, safe limit and risk all inherit this.
suggested_fix: Fill zero months up to the last complete month ($currentMonthStart->copy()->subMonth()), not just up to the last populated month, so the series ends right before the target period. Update the use-case doc and add a test with a history that ends several months before the current month.
verifier_notes: generate() fills zero months only between the first and last populated month (line 97-106); financial_forecasting.py also uses only the given records with x relative to the first month and target_period far ahead, so trailing quiet months are lost and extrapolation spans the gap. sample_months = monthly->count() reflects the shortened series.

title: Stored advice goes stale after ledger changes and contradicts the recomputed risk badge
evidence: 'overspending_risk' => Budget::overspendingRiskFor((float) $current + $delta, (float) $budget->warning_threshold),  // advisory_note, recommended_allocation, safe_spending_limit and the BUDGET_EXPLANATION AiOutput are left untouched; FinancePage.jsx:1491 shows `{sentence(b.overspending_risk)} overspending risk` next to `{b.advisory_note}` (1500)
impact: Each later transaction or approval (ApprovalRequestController:370) rewrites overspending_risk on a different scale: remaining <= threshold gives 'medium', while the engine gives 'high'. The advisory_note, recommended allocation, safe ceiling and advice_details still describe the old numbers. A budget can show 'Low overspending risk' above 'A deficit is projected. Pause discretionary spending...'. The DashboardInsightEngine budgetRisk card titles itself from the new risk and uses the old note as its body. advice_generated_at is never shown on the budget row.
suggested_fix: When remaining_amount, allocated_amount or warning_threshold changes, clear advisory_note, recommended_allocation, safe_spending_limit and advice_generated_at, or mark the advice stale. On the client, show 'Advice from <date>' and a 'Get advice again' prompt when advice_generated_at is older than the budget's updated_at. Use one risk scale for both writers.
verifier_notes: TransactionController::applyBudgetMovement and ApprovalRequestController:370 rewrite overspending_risk via Budget::overspendingRiskFor (remaining<=threshold -> medium) while advisory_note, recommended_allocation, safe_spending_limit, advice_generated_at stay. DashboardInsightEngine:102-103 titles from the new risk and uses the old note as body; FinancePage 1491/1500 shows both side by side.

title: Budget advice silently uses zeros or a stale or manual forecast, and the success message still says 'from the latest forecast'
evidence: return static::where('organization_id', $organizationId)->orderByDesc('updated_at')->orderByDesc('id')->first();  // BudgetController: 'predicted_income' => (float) ($forecast?->predicted_income ?? 0); FinancePage.jsx:790 showFeedback('success', 'Budget advice generated from the latest forecast and available funds.')
impact: With no forecast, predicted income and expense become 0. The advice then reports 'The projection is stable' and the explanation is told to cite forecast income and expense that do not exist. latestFor picks whichever row was edited last, so a hand-edited 'Q4 2024' manual row, or a forecast for a month long past, drives today's advice. The client never shows which forecast or period was used; forecast_id is returned but ignored.
suggested_fix: Only use a forecast whose Y-m period is the current or next month. If none exists, return 409 'Generate a forecast first' or set forecast_status 'missing' and leave out the forecast terms. Return and show the forecast period with the advice, and change the success message to match what was used.
verifier_notes: latestFor orders by updated_at with no period check; with no forecast, predicted_income/expense default to 0; FinancePage:790 always says "from the latest forecast"; forecast_id is returned but unused on the client.

title: Department Head forecast view mixes every college organization's forecasts into one chart and list with no organization label
evidence: canViewForecasts ? fetchAllPages((p) => getForecasts(p).then((r) => r.data), organizationScope) ...  // organizationScope is {} while organizationFilter === '' (line 491); FinancialForecastController::index loads only 'generator', not 'organization'
impact: A head opening Financial insights with the default 'all organizations' filter sees one line chart. It joins Org A's and Org B's December forecasts into a single income, expense and balance series, with duplicate x-labels and duplicate React keys (FinancialForecastChart.jsx:36). The list shows several 'Forecast for 2026-12' cards and gives no way to tell which organization each belongs to, so the oversight job cannot be done reliably.
suggested_fix: Eager load organization:id,name,acronym in index(), print the organization on each card, and for a Department Head without an organization filter either group by organization (one chart each) or require a selection before drawing the chart.
verifier_notes: canViewForecasts = canReadFinance; GET /forecasts allows DEPARTMENT_HEAD; readableOrganizationIds returns every scoped id when no organization_id is sent (organizationFilter defaults to ''). index() eager loads only generator. FinancialForecastChart keys points by label, so duplicate periods produce duplicate keys; the list uses f.id so only the chart keys collide.

title: Current available budget sums approved budgets from every semester, including closed ones
impact: Leftover remaining_amount on last semester's approved event budgets, and their warning thresholds, are added to 'current available'. This inflates the safe spending limit and can turn a deficit into 'stable'. The Budgets tab is semester scoped (SemesterScope::budgets), so the figure in model_details.current_available_budget does not match any total the Admin can see.
suggested_fix: Apply SemesterScope::budgets($query, AcademicSemester::active()) (or the selected semester) to $approvedBudgets, sum per budget with recomputedRemaining()-style SQL rather than the cached column, and store the semester id in model_details.
verifier_notes: The approved-budget sum in generate() has no semester scope, unlike the semester-scoped Budgets tab, so closed-semester leftovers inflate current_available_budget and warning_threshold. The part of the fix about not using the cached column is unsupported: remaining_amount is maintained by applyBudgetMovement and approval, and already includes income posted against the budget.
corrected_fix: Scope $approvedBudgets with SemesterScope::budgets($query, AcademicSemester::active()) and record the semester id in model_details; keep summing remaining_amount.

title: Financial report AI summary includes advisories from unapproved budgets and from outside the report period, plus an unrelated latest forecast
impact: $semester is null for monthly and custom reports, so every budget that ever received advice is included, whatever its date. No submission_status filter is applied, so pending and rejected budgets' advisory notes and safe ceilings go into the summary sent to the Department Head. A report for Semester 1 also quotes whichever forecast was edited last, for example December 2026. The summary prompt asks the model to describe 'the latest forecast and any budget advisory results' as part of the period.
suggested_fix: Filter budgets with where('submission_status','approved') and advice_generated_at between $start and $end (or SemesterScope for every report type). Pick the forecast whose Y-m period falls inside the report period, or none, and say 'no forecast for this period'.
verifier_notes: $semester is null unless academic_semester_id is given (line 134-136), and SemesterScope::budgets returns the query unchanged for null; there is no submission_status filter and no date filter on advice_generated_at; latestFor picks the last-edited forecast regardless of the report period.

title: Forecast explanation omits current funds, so a safe limit far above the projected balance is shown unexplained, and manual forecasts use a different formula
impact: The generated safe limit is (current approved funds + income - expense) x 0.8, but neither the AI prompt nor the fallback sentence names the current funds. Example: income 10,000, expense 8,000, balance 2,000, current 50,000 gives a safe limit of 41,600. The card and summary say 'balance PHP 2,000 ... safe spending limit PHP 41,600' with no reason. A manually created forecast with the same income and expense stores a safe limit of 1,600, so the same column means two different things on one chart.
suggested_fix: Add current_available_budget, and the estimated available budget from the advice, to the prompt, the facts and the fallback sentence ('With PHP 50,000 in approved budgets...'). Show it on the forecast card. Use the same formula in deriveForecastFields, or label manual rows.
verifier_notes: financialSummary() gets only period, income, expense, balance, safeLimit and risk; the safe limit comes from advice computed with current_available_budget, which neither the prompt nor the fallback mentions. deriveForecastFields uses max(0, income-expense)*0.8 for manual rows.

title: FinancialForecastController's PHP fallback rates risk differently from the Python engine and BudgetController's fallback
impact: Example: income 1,000, expense 500, current 0, threshold 600. Python and BudgetController::localBudgetAdvice return high. This fallback returns medium with the advice text 'Spending risk is elevated' instead of Python's wording. Whether the engine is up changes the stored model_details.budget_advice, and AiFallbackParityTest has no case for the warning threshold.
suggested_fix: Move the advice rules into one PHP class (reuse BudgetController's version, which matches Python), call it from both controllers, and add a live parity test for the warning-threshold and ratio >= 0.9 branches.
verifier_notes: FinancialForecastController::localBudgetAdvice line 440 maps overspending caused by the warning threshold to medium unless expense>income; advise_budget and BudgetController::localBudgetAdvice return high for the threshold branch. The worked example (1000/500/0/600) gives high vs medium. Advice wording also differs from Python in both PHP fallbacks.

title: Manual forecasts accept a free-text period and client-supplied model_details, then feed advice and the dashboard as if they were generated
impact: An Admin can post model_details {engine:'python-fastapi', fit_quality:'strong', is_reliable:true}, and the UI shows it as a reliable model run. Without model_details, DashboardInsightEngine::forecastTrend uses `$details['risk'] ?? 'stable'`, so a manual forecast with predicted_balance -5,000 appears on the dashboard as 'Financial forecast for X: stable'. Because it becomes latestFor, it also drives per-budget advice.
suggested_fix: Validate forecast_period as date_format:Y-m. Drop model_details from the input and have the server write {engine:'manual', risk: derived from balance and the advice rules}. Exclude engine === 'manual' from latestFor for advice, or label it clearly.
verifier_notes: Real: manual forecasts (Admin only) accept free-text forecast_period and arbitrary model_details, and DashboardInsightEngine::forecastTrend defaults risk to stable, so a negative-balance manual forecast shows as stable and also becomes latestFor for advice. The model_details spoofing is the org Admin describing their own data, so it is a data-integrity gap, not a privilege issue. date_format:Y-m on update would reject edits to older free-text rows unless the period is left out.
corrected_fix: Strip model_details from input and have store/update write {engine:'manual', risk derived from predicted_balance with the advice rules}; validate forecast_period as date_format:Y-m on store (and on update only when present); exclude manual rows from latestFor for advice or label them.

title: Forecast card never shows predicted expense
impact: The chart, which is hidden below 640px, is the only place predicted expense appears. On phones the card shows income and balance but not the expense the balance and risk were derived from, even though the summary text talks about expected expenses.
verifier_notes: The forecast card dl (FinancePage ~1590) lists Income, Balance, Safe spend and Risk only; the chart, the only other place expense appears, is hidden below sm.

title: Budget advice can be generated and stored for pending or rejected budgets
evidence: $budget = Budget::with('event:id,title')->where('organization_id', $request->user()->organization_id)->find($id);  // no submission_status check before writing recommended_allocation / safe_spending_limit
impact: Only approved budgets count as available, but an unapproved budget gets a 'Recommended allocation' and a 'Safe spending ceiling' as if its money could be spent. Those advisories then reach financial report summaries (see finance-ai-07).
suggested_fix: Return 409 'Advice is available once the budget is approved' unless submission_status === 'approved', and hide 'Get advice' for other statuses on the client.
verifier_notes: advice() and the client Get advice action have no submission_status gate, so pending/rejected budgets get stored advice. Advice on a draft can be legitimate planning, so the harm is mostly that it reaches report summaries and the dashboard as if final (covered by finance-ai-07).
corrected_fix: Either gate advice to approved budgets (409 otherwise, hide Get advice), or allow it as pre-approval planning but label it as such and exclude non-approved budgets from report summaries and dashboard insights.
